requirements.evidence: The migrations implement every required column, index and generated column (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:14-21, database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:14-27). The contract is present: Entity has SoftDeletes, getRouteKeyName(), memberships(), users() and owner() (app/Models/Entity.php:18-49); EntityMembership has the role cast, scopes and relations (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:23-68); UserRole has manageable() (app/Models/UserRole.php:7-18); User has memberships(), entities() and membershipFor() (app/Models/User.php:41-59); factories and both policies exist (database/factories/EntityFactory.php:18-24, database/factories/EntityMembershipFactory.php:21-43, app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-43, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-41).

conventions.evidence: Generated-style migrations with reversible down() methods (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:7-31, database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:7-37), deliberate #[Fillable] attributes (app/Models/Entity.php:14, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:12), and policies used for authorization follow the project conventions. However, docs/database-schema.md:151 still says the one-user-per-entity rule is enforced in the application, docs/database-schema.md:34 still lists an unimplemented entities.locale_default, docs/database-schema.md:140 still labels the owner relation 1:1, CHANGELOG.md is not updated, and app/Models/User.php:56 lacks the PHPDoc the other new model methods carry.

security.evidence: Authorization is entirely server-side policy logic: EntityPolicy checks membership and owner/admin roles (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:16-34) and EntityMembershipPolicy checks same-entity membership, owner/admin assignment and the owner/self-removal delete rules (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-41). Owner uniqueness is enforced by the database rather than trusted application logic (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:18-27). No user input, output rendering or secrets are introduced by this diff; no security weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:24-114 covers route-key/soft deletes, factory defaults, relations, index names, the second-owner rejection (including promotion via update), multi-entity owners, duplicate membership rejection and the user-delete cascade; tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:116-179 exercises every policy method across owner, admin, employee, outsider and other-entity actors and checks policy auto-discovery. Two schema behaviors remain untested: entity-delete cascading memberships and the slug unique constraint actually rejecting duplicates.

simplicity.evidence: The change uses standard Eloquent relations and a native database generated column instead of custom abstractions (app/Models/Entity.php:36-49, database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:18-27), adds no service/repository layers, and keeps the two policies small and direct (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-43, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-41).

readability.evidence: Names and method structure are clear, relation/scopes/casts are documented with generics (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:18-67), policies read top-to-bottom, and the test file groups behavior into focused Pest cases with a small memberOf helper (tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:16-22).

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: models and enum under app/Models, policies under app/Policies, factories and migrations, the schema doc, and one feature test. No routes, Livewire components, pages, session handling or other out-of-scope features were added.

issues.explanation: The note still says the one-user-per-entity rule is enforced in the application, but the new unique index entity_memberships_entity_user_unique now enforces it in the database, so the schema doc is not fully in sync with the implementation.

The ER diagram still lists entities.locale_default although the implemented entities migration does not create that column, and the owner relationship row still says 1 : 1 although the note and schema allow zero owners; both make the newly marked 'implemented' schema slightly misleading.
The project conventions require a Keep a Changelog entry under [Unreleased] for each change, and no CHANGELOG update is included.

The suite verifies index names and the user-delete cascade, but never asserts that a duplicate slug is rejected or that deleting an entity cascades its memberships, leaving two required schema behaviors untested.
The new public membershipFor() method has no PHPDoc, unlike the other new model methods, despite the convention to add PHPDoc on public methods touched.

review.summary: The change adds the complete entity/membership schema with the generated owner-uniqueness constraint, Eloquent models, the UserRole enum, factories, authorization policies and a broad Pest suite, and updates the database schema doc. The implementation is solid and well tested, but stale schema-doc statements, a missing CHANGELOG entry and two untested schema edge cases (entity-delete cascade and slug uniqueness) make it an approve-with-nits rather than a clean pass.
